children: Mexican fintech Kontempo announced on Tuesday it had raised $10.5 million to expand a trade-credit platform used by industrial groups including cementmaker Cemex
, betting large manufacturers and their distributor networks need better tools to sell more goods across Mexico's economy.

Kontempo works in the business-to-business credit market that props up sales of construction material, chemicals and packaging supplies. It helps suppliers and distributors offer short-term payment terms to business buyers, while handling credit analysis, collections, payments reconciliation and financing.
Trade credit, in which one business allows another to pay later for goods, is a critical but often overlooked part of Mexico's industrial economy, founder and CEO Matthew Meehan said.
He estimated that roughly one-third of Mexico's economy is tied to industrial activity and that a large share of those transactions are conducted on credit.
Kontempo works primarily with distributors and wholesale buyers rather than consumers.
The company says it has processed more than $180 million in transactions since launching in 2022 and expects volume to exceed $200 million this year. It forecasts triple-digit growth in 2027.

Meehan said distributors using the platform typically approve about 70% of credit applicants, compared with around 10% to 20% before adopting the technology. Kontempo has seen sales increases of 30% to 40% among some distributors using its products, he said.

The fresh capital will be used to expand beyond large corporate clients into Mexico's mid-sized business market and roll out AI-powered products, including credit-scoring tools and virtual credit and collections agents.
